specification:
Type: microsim **sim-id:** study-plan-classifier
**Library:** p5.js
**Status:** Specified
**Bloom Level:** Understand
**Bloom Verb:** classify
**Learning Objective:** The learner will classify each of six study plans by what the learner does (retrieval practice or rereading) and by when (spaced or massed), with at least 10 of 12 judgments correct on the first attempt. **Prerequisites:** Retrieval Practice, Spaced Practice, Formative Assessment (all defined in this chapter above this block). **Evidence of Mastery:** For each plan the learner makes two judgments, one about the activity and one about the timing. A judgment is correct when it matches the Content table. Mastery is at least 10 of 12 judgments correct on the first attempt. Reading the definitions is exploration, not evidence. **Misconceptions:** (1) Rereading counts as retrieval practice. (2) Highlighting is a form of testing. (3) Any practice done over several days is spaced practice. **Instructional Rationale:** Classifying a plan on two features is an Understand-level action that separates the two ideas learners often merge. Six plans that cross the two features teach the learner that retrieval and spacing are independent. **Content:** The two judgments for each plan: Activity (Retrieval practice, where the learner tries to recall without looking, or Rereading, where the learner looks at material again) and Timing (Spaced, with gaps of a day or more between sessions, or Massed, all in one sitting or the night before). The six plans: | # | Plan shown to the learner | Activity | Timing | Why (shown as feedback) | |---|---|---|---|---| | 1 | Read the chapter three times the night before the test. | Rereading | Massed | The learner looks at the text again, and does it all at once. | | 2 | Close the book and write down everything you remember, then check. Do it the day after reading and again a week later. | Retrieval practice | Spaced | The learner recalls without looking, with gaps between sessions. | | 3 | Highlight the chapter on Monday and reread the highlights on Tuesday and Friday. | Rereading | Spaced | The learner looks at material again, with gaps between sessions. | | 4 | Make flash cards and quiz yourself on all of them for three hours the evening before the exam. | Retrieval practice | Massed | The learner recalls without looking, all in one sitting. | | 5 | Take a five-question quiz at the start of each class on last week's material. | Retrieval practice | Spaced | The learner recalls without looking, a week later and each week. | | 6 | Copy your notes neatly the weekend before the test. | Rereading | Massed | Copying is a form of looking again, done in one stretch. | **Provenance:** The plans are illustrative cases written for this chapter, and the sim labels them "illustrative examples". The definitions follow the chapter sections "Retrieval Practice" and "Spaced Practice". **Rules:** Each plan has exactly one correct activity and one correct timing, so the sim holds 12 judgments. Three plans are Retrieval practice and three are Rereading. Three are Spaced and three are Massed. **Learner Activity:** 1. The learner sees one plan and two questions. 2. The learner chooses the activity and the timing, and both choices are committed together. 3. The sim shows whether each was correct and the Why text. 4. After plan 6 the sim shows the summary. **Feedback:** 6 plans in a shuffled order, one attempt each. Correct: "Correct: [activity], [timing]. [Why]". Incorrect: "Not quite. This plan is [activity] and [timing]. [Why]". The summary shows "[n] of 12 judgments correct on the first attempt". At 10 or more it adds "You can tell recall from rereading and spacing from cramming." Below 10 it lists the Why text of each missed plan. **Starting State:** The first plan and the two questions, "What does the learner do?" and "When?" **Chapter Anchors:** The chapter defines retrieval practice as recalling without looking and spaced practice as gaps between sessions, and says rereading is not retrieval.
